headline: High: shared-state orchestration plus broad egress creates default risks of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors; compliance risk is moderate.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LangGraph can pass state between nodes and instances via a checkpointer store, while Plane accepts files/notes/issues and broad egress. If LangGraph ingests Plane content as node input, attacker-controlled text can steer downstream instructions. The pairwise bridge is documented only indirectly, so uncertainty stays medium rather than low.
conditions: IF LangGraph nodes read Plane-uploaded notes or files as prompts or tool instructions, injection is possible.
IF the shared checkpointer or workspace is writable by both agents, attacker text can persist across runs.
mitigations: Separate Plane uploads from LangGraph prompt inputs.
Add content-tagging so only trusted fields become instructions.
Disable automatic parsing of notes/files as commands.
Use a read-only handoff format with explicit allowlists.
requires-engineering: add provenance tracking in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: LangGraph handles model-provider API keys and can read/write application files; Plane touches issues, tasks, files, images, and notes with file uploads. A shared workspace or checkpointer can expose sensitive work products to both agents, and LangGraph's broad egress increases the chance of unintended transmission. The interaction is plausible in default deployments, though not directly reproduced.
conditions: IF both agents share the same filesystem, Plane artifacts can be read by LangGraph.
IF LangGraph forwards file contents to model providers, shared work products may leave the boundary.
mitigations: Place each agent in a separate workspace.
Restrict LangGraph to least-privilege file paths.
Block automatic upload of Plane files to inference APIs.
Rotate and isolate API keys per agent.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage and egress policies.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LangGraph can execute shell commands, spawn subprocesses, and write files; Plane does not write filesystems but does support broad egress and file uploads. The main conflict is not direct write-write collision, but shared mutable state through the checkpointer or application files can still cause races and overwrites. Because the orchestrator supports multiple instances, coordination is needed.
conditions: IF both agents target the same application directory, LangGraph can overwrite Plane-managed artifacts.
IF the checkpointer store is shared without locking, concurrent runs can race on state.
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories to each agent.
Enable locking around shared state writes.
Run Plane as read-only to LangGraph.
Serialize writes through one coordinator.
requires-engineering: add transactional state updates.

D_cascading_error.rationale: LangGraph is a low-level orchestration framework where node outputs can become later node inputs, and Plane stores issues, tasks, and notes that may be acted on downstream. If Plane treats LangGraph-generated text as authoritative, a mistaken or malicious output can cascade into incorrect tasking or scheduling. The pairwise pathway is inferred from documented roles, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Plane ingests LangGraph-generated summaries without verification, errors can propagate.
IF LangGraph automates actions from Plane records, a single bad record can cascade across workflows.
mitigations: Require human review before Plane actions.
Add schema validation on LangGraph outputs.
Cross-check critical fields against source records.
Log and flag low-confidence outputs.
requires-engineering: implement verification gates between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and do not declare PHI, residency, or certification constraints, so no direct compliance breach is evidenced. However, Plane handles files and notes while LangGraph can handle model-provider API keys and broad egress, so a deployment could create policy mismatch if sensitive data is routed through external providers. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise deployment-related.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Plane and then routed through LangGraph to external model providers, policy controls may be violated.
IF the deployment requires residency or retention guarantees, neither profile documents them.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Use self-hosted model endpoints only.
Document retention and deletion settings.
Review vendor DPAs before deployment.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention enforcement.
